verdict: CooperCompanies grew revenue just 1% to $1.07B, but a $307M one-off tax benefit lifted net income to $433M — more than four times a year ago — while its contact-lens business deliberately shrank U.S. inventory.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $1.07B in revenue, vs $1.06B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.49 a year ago — lifted by the one-off tax benefit

kpis.label: One-off tax benefit
kpis.note: Discrete benefit from completing a UK tax examination — see one-off items

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Up 66% YoY — $342M of operating cash flow minus $69M of capital spending

segments.name: CooperVision
segments.note: Contact lenses — toric and multifocal lenses rose 2% organically while standard lenses fell 1%. Revenue was flat as the company proactively reduced U.S. channel inventory, which will also weigh on the fourth quarter.

segments.name: CooperSurgical
segments.note: Medical devices for women's health and surgery — office and surgical products $208M (+2% organically) and fertility products $141M (+5% organically).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling lenses and devices and running the company — down from $422M a year ago on expense management.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of past acquisitions over time.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new lenses and devices — down slightly from $45M a year ago.

follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.

takeaways.title: A tax settlement did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Net income jumped to $433M from $98M a year ago almost entirely because of a $307M discrete tax benefit: the UK tax authority (HMRC) finished examining Cooper's 2021 transfer of intellectual property to the UK, and a reserve set aside for it was released. The total tax line was a $231M benefit.

takeaways.title: Contact lenses stood still — on purpose
takeaways.text: CooperVision revenue was flat at $717M as the company proactively cut U.S. channel inventory, a drag it says will continue into the fourth quarter. CooperSurgical grew 2% to $349M, and overall gross margin improved to 67% from 65%.

takeaways.title: Cash is going to buybacks
takeaways.text: Free cash flow rose 66% to $273M, and Cooper repurchased $339M of its own stock in the quarter. The board expanded the buyback authorization from $2B to $3B, with about $1.5B still available.

oneTimers: A $307.2M discrete tax benefit from the favorable completion of HMRC's examination of the fiscal 2021 transfer of intellectual property and related assets to the United Kingdom — it reverses a reserve recorded in 2021 and is the primary driver of the quarter's $231M total tax benefit and the jump in GAAP EPS to $2.24.
Smaller items the company excludes from non-GAAP results include $4.3M of strategic review costs and $2.2M of litigation expense and associated legal costs in the quarter.
otherDetail: Other expense of $20M, net: $21.5M of interest expense, partly offset by $1.3M of other income (figures rounded to $M).
footerNote: CooperCompanies reports to one decimal place in $M; figures here are rounded to whole $M so the lines balance (net income was $432.8M as reported). Its fiscal year ends October 31, so this is the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
